title: AI strategy and opportunity assessment
description: Prioritise worthwhile AI opportunities, assess readiness and build a practical investment case and roadmap around business value.
body:
Start with a business decision

An AI strategy should help you decide where to invest, what to test, and what to leave alone. We start with the work your business needs to improve: a slow handoff, a knowledge bottleneck, a repetitive review, or a service experience that depends on scarce expertise.

Our role is to connect that operational context with realistic options. A useful recommendation considers your systems, the information available, the people who will use the solution, and the consequences when it gets something wrong.

Find the opportunities worth investigating

We work with leadership and the people closest to the workflow to understand how work happens today. What enters the process? Which decisions require judgement? Where do exceptions accumulate? Which steps create waiting, rework, or inconsistent output?

From there, we develop an opportunity shortlist. Each candidate needs an owner, a clear purpose, a plausible approach, and evidence that the problem matters. We assess value alongside feasibility and uncertainty, so an exciting idea does not outrank a more useful one simply because it is easier to demonstrate.

What the engagement can cover

  • Leadership and workflow discovery to establish the problem and decision context.
  • An opportunity inventory with the assumptions and evidence behind each candidate.
  • Readiness review covering information quality, systems access, ownership, and adoption needs.
  • Build, buy, or adapt options, including the implications of existing tools.
  • A phased roadmap and a brief for the next pilot or procurement decision.

A roadmap your organisation can act on

The output should be understandable to the executive sponsor and useful to the people responsible for implementation. We explain the recommendation, its trade-offs, dependencies, and open questions. Where evidence is weak, the next step may be a discovery task rather than a build.

A roadmap can include quick operational improvements as well as more ambitious projects. We make the relationship between them explicit: which early work creates knowledge, access, or habits that a later project will need?

Decide what success would mean before the pilot

We help define a baseline and the observations needed to judge the next step. Those might include the quality of an answer, the handling of exceptions, the time involved in a specific step, or whether people can use the workflow effectively. The right measures depend on the job the system is meant to do.

Expected benefits remain assumptions until tested. We make cost, volume, review effort, and adoption assumptions visible, and use ranges where a single forecast would suggest more certainty than the evidence supports.

Make the investment case explicit

Across a portfolio, opportunities compete for funding, specialist time, and the attention of the people affected. We help compare those demands, identify shared dependencies, and make the basis for an investment decision clear.

A useful business case records the current baseline, expected improvement, total operating effort, adoption assumptions, and the evidence still needed. It also names an owner for reviewing benefits as the work progresses. Our article on measuring AI value beyond usage explains how to keep those assumptions connected to business outcomes.

How we work with your team

We agree a project scope around the decision you need to make. Your leadership provides sponsorship and context; workflow owners bring practical knowledge; technical colleagues contribute constraints and access requirements. Authentia brings structure, analysis, and recommendations across those perspectives.

You retain authority over priorities and investment. Your internal team or implementation partner can use the resulting brief to plan delivery, with Authentia available for continuing advice.

A useful starting point

Bring a business objective, one or two troublesome workflows, and any evidence you already have. You do not need a model preference or a finished project specification. If you want to prepare first, start with our AI Opportunity Scorecard.

An AI value and investment review can be a focused starting point when you need to compare existing initiatives, test their assumptions, and decide where further investment is justified.
answer: Authentia helps leaders prioritise AI opportunities, compare options and build a practical investment roadmap. We connect business objectives with workflow evidence, organisational readiness, expected value and delivery dependencies. The engagement produces decision briefs and a phased plan that your internal team or implementation partner can use.

title: AI and digital change management
description: Prepare people and workflows for new technology with clear ownership, stakeholder alignment, practical enablement and adoption measures.
answer: AI and digital change management prepares people and workflows for new technology. Authentia helps sponsors assess readiness and role impacts, align stakeholders, plan practical communication and learning, and define adoption measures. Your organisation owns delivery; our advisory work gives leaders and programme teams a clear plan and decision support.
body:
Make the change workable for the people doing it

A new tool can be available before teams understand when to use it, how their work changes, or who owns the result. A pilot may demonstrate a useful capability while managers still need a clearer plan for introducing it into daily operations.

AI and digital change management brings these questions into the implementation plan. Authentia helps leaders assess the change, prepare the people affected, and give programme teams a practical way forward. The engagement can support an AI initiative or a related change to a customer platform, internal system, or business process.

Understand readiness and the impact on each role

We begin with the current workflow and the people who perform, manage, and support it. What will change in their tasks and decisions? Which skills, information, or access will they need? What other changes are competing for their attention?

A readiness and impact review makes those differences visible across roles and teams. For AI, it also considers where people must check an output, handle an exception, or decide that the tool is unsuitable for a task. These requirements inform the rollout, learning plan, and support arrangements.

For organisations managing several initiatives, we can help sponsors sequence the changes and identify common enablement needs. This makes demands on the same teams visible and gives programme leads a basis for agreeing practical priorities.

Give sponsors and managers a useful plan

We help sponsors agree the purpose of the change, the decisions that need their involvement, and what managers should be able to explain to their teams. Stakeholder planning identifies the people affected, the concerns to investigate, and the owners who can resolve them.

Communication should answer practical questions: what is changing, why it matters, what people are expected to do, and where they can get help. We can develop a communication approach and manager briefing materials with your programme team, with your organisation responsible for approval and delivery.

Plan learning around the work

People need opportunities to practise the tasks they will actually perform. We help shape role-based learning, realistic examples, and guidance for reviewing AI output or dealing with incomplete information. Leadership sessions can help sponsors and managers work through the decisions their teams will face.

Training belongs within a broader adoption plan. That plan should connect learning with access, workable processes, manager support, feedback, and a clear response when the new approach creates a problem. Our article on AI adoption beyond training explores those connections.

What the engagement can produce

  • A change brief defining the purpose, affected groups, dependencies, and decisions ahead.
  • A readiness and role-impact assessment with priorities for preparation.
  • A sponsor and stakeholder plan with clear ownership and engagement needs.
  • A communication and enablement plan, with manager briefings and practical learning priorities.
  • An adoption review framework covering evidence, feedback, measures, and review responsibilities.

Review adoption and keep a clear owner

Adoption measures should reflect the job the change is meant to improve. Alongside appropriate use, we help teams consider output quality, review effort, service outcomes, exceptions, confidence, and unresolved workarounds. The baseline and review points should be agreed before wider rollout.

Your sponsor and programme leads own implementation, internal communication, learning delivery, and ongoing operation. Authentia provides analysis, facilitation, planning, and decision support within an agreed remit. Where the process itself needs attention, our workflow and operating model design service can help define the work people are being asked to adopt.

title: Workflow and operating model design
short: Define how the work should run
description: Connect people, systems and AI through practical workflows, clear decision rights, useful handoffs and responsibilities your team can implement.
answer: Authentia helps organisations redesign how work moves between people, systems and AI. We map the current process, clarify decisions and exceptions, define future roles and handoffs, and prepare a practical operating model. Your team receives a shared workflow design, responsibility map and transition priorities for implementation.
body:
Design the work around the outcome

Improving one task can change the demands on the rest of a process. Faster drafting may create a review queue. An automated handoff may move incomplete information into another team. A useful AI capability needs a workflow that makes the whole job manageable.

Authentia helps leaders and operational teams define that workflow. We connect the business outcome with the people, systems, information, and decisions needed to achieve it. The resulting design gives your organisation a shared basis for implementation and the responsibilities that follow.

Map what happens today

We work with the people who perform and own the process to understand how work actually moves. What starts it? Which inputs are required? Where does it wait? Who makes decisions, and what happens when a normal route does not fit?

The review considers handoffs between functions as well as individual tasks. We record known volumes, review effort, exceptions, information gaps, and dependencies, with the evidence available. Differences between the documented process and daily practice become questions to resolve with the relevant owners.

Define a future workflow people can use

A future workflow should explain the job of each step and the conditions under which it can proceed. We help define where AI could retrieve, classify, draft, or recommend, and where a person should approve, exercise judgement, or take responsibility for an action.

That includes the less visible parts of the process: how an output is checked, who handles an unfamiliar case, which information may be used, and how work returns to a person when a tool is unavailable. Scenario walkthroughs help the team examine these decisions before committing to implementation.

Connect processes, roles and information

An operating model makes the responsibilities around the workflow explicit. Who owns the process and its outcomes? Who maintains the knowledge the system uses? Who manages access, resolves exceptions, and decides whether a proposed change is acceptable?

We help clarify these relationships across operational, technology, and supporting functions. The design can include decision rights, review arrangements, service expectations, and the information owners need. Where changes affect roles or organisational structures, your leadership and relevant people teams retain those decisions.

What the engagement can produce

  • A current-workflow map with documented friction, dependencies, and evidence gaps.
  • A future-workflow design covering human decisions, AI assistance, handoffs, and exceptions.
  • A responsibility and decision-rights map for the process and its ongoing support.
  • Operating requirements for information, review, access, knowledge maintenance, and service continuity.
  • Transition priorities and a brief that your implementation team or provider can use.

Make the transition practical

We help identify which changes depend on each other and what should be tested first. Some issues may be resolved through clearer ownership or a simpler process. Others may require a technology decision, better information, or a different allocation of work. The recommendation explains those choices and the assumptions behind them.

The workflow design should also inform change management and enablement. Teams need to understand their responsibilities, practise the new tasks, and know how to raise an issue. Governance requirements belong in the design so the process reflects the decisions the organisation has agreed.

Authentia provides analysis, workshops, and recommendations. Your organisation owns implementation, role and structural decisions, technical delivery, and ongoing operation. Start with one important process or a connected set of handoffs; our Workflow Brief Template can help describe the work and the decision you need to make.

title: Practical AI governance
description: Give teams practical guidance for AI decisions, with clear ownership, review routes, human oversight and escalation alongside your existing specialist functions.
answer: Practical AI governance establishes who can approve AI use, which information and actions are permitted, and when people must review or intervene. Authentia helps teams define workable guidance, decision rights, oversight and escalation. We coordinate the questions with your legal, privacy, security and technical owners, who retain their specialist responsibilities.
body:
Give people a clear way to make AI decisions

As more teams consider AI, they need a shared understanding of what can be used, who can approve it, and what requires closer review. Sponsors need to know which decisions are being made across the organisation and where responsibilities remain unresolved.

Practical governance connects the organisation's principles with the workflows people use. Authentia helps leaders and relevant functions translate those principles into clear guidance, ownership, review routes, and decision records. The work is shaped around the AI uses your organisation is considering or already managing.

Start with actual use cases and owners

We help establish a useful view of proposed and current AI uses: their purpose, intended users, information sources, outputs, actions, and business owners. Understanding the workflow makes it easier for the appropriate specialists to assess the questions that matter.

The review also identifies the people affected by an AI-supported decision and the consequences of a mistake. We help teams agree which proposals need which reviews, what evidence those reviews require, and who can authorise the next step. The review route should fit the intended use and your existing policies.

Translate principles into everyday guidance

Teams need guidance they can apply to a real task. Which tools and information sources have been approved? What should a person check before using an output? When should work be referred to a specialist, and what should happen when an answer is uncertain or inappropriate?

We can help develop working guidance and decision tools with your operational and specialist owners. This can include acceptable-use guidance, role responsibilities, human review points, and escalation arrangements. It should connect with existing procurement, information management, security, privacy, and incident processes.

Make decisions and reviews traceable

A decision record should explain the intended use, the evidence considered, the conditions of approval, and the person responsible for the next review. Assumptions and unresolved questions should remain visible to the people who will rely on the decision.

We help define review points when an AI use changes: a different model or provider, a new information source, broader access, or a more consequential action. The organisation can then decide which changes require fresh evaluation and which can follow an established route. Your responsible teams manage the controls and the evidence they produce.

What the engagement can produce

  • An initial AI-use inventory and practical priorities for further review.
  • A decision-rights map covering proposal ownership, review, approval, and escalation.
  • Acceptable-use guidance linked to defined roles and workflows.
  • Review questions for tools and providers, including information use, oversight, operating responsibilities, and ability to change direction.
  • Human-review and issue-escalation arrangements that connect with existing procedures.
  • Decision-record templates and an agreed cadence for revisiting assumptions and conditions.

Work alongside the functions that own the decisions

Authentia brings structure, facilitation, and business context to this work. Your legal and privacy advisers determine applicable obligations and interpretations. Security and technical owners assess their requirements and implement controls. Business sponsors and governance owners retain approval and accountability for the organisation's AI use.

We help those perspectives meet in a practical process that programme teams can follow. The scope can focus on one initiative or a shared approach across related uses. Our implementation and pilot advisory can support the decisions a particular project needs, while change management helps prepare the people who will apply the guidance in daily work.

title: Implementation and pilot advisory
description: Shape a bounded pilot, compare tools and providers, and review delivery plans and evidence before deciding whether to expand.
body:
Carry the strategy into real decisions

A promising use case introduces a new set of questions once a team starts planning implementation. Which capabilities should an existing product provide? What information should the system use? Where should a person review its output? What would justify expanding beyond a pilot?

Authentia supports the sponsor and delivery team through these decisions. We help translate the intended business outcome into a scope that a technical team or provider can assess, build, and evaluate.

Give the pilot a clear job

A pilot needs to resolve an uncertainty. It may test whether a product can use the right knowledge, whether a workflow fits daily operations, or whether review effort leaves a worthwhile benefit. Defining that purpose helps prevent a demonstration from becoming an open-ended implementation.

We help set the intended users, information sources, boundaries, and exceptions. A good pilot brief records what is included, what will wait, and what should happen when the proposed approach does not work.

Make tool and provider choices in context

We can help you develop evaluation questions, compare approaches, and review proposals against the workflow. A feature list is only part of that decision. Existing systems, access controls, knowledge maintenance, export options, running costs, and the team's ability to operate the solution all matter.

Where possible, evaluation should use representative work rather than an idealised demonstration. We help clarify which claims a provider needs to substantiate and which assumptions the client needs to test.

Where we can contribute

  • A pilot charter with scope, intended users, dependencies, and decision criteria.
  • Tool and provider evaluation, with a record of trade-offs and open questions.
  • Workflow and integration planning alongside your technical colleagues.
  • Review of evaluation examples, escalation routes, and human review points.
  • Implementation briefings and decision support for the delivery team.
  • Results review and a recommendation to expand, revise, investigate, or stop.

Keep responsibilities visible

In an advisory engagement, your team or implementation partner owns delivery and operation. We provide analysis, challenge, and guidance within an agreed scope. The sponsor owns business decisions, technical owners manage system access and implementation, and workflow owners help establish whether the change works in practice.

We make those responsibilities explicit at the beginning. Advice about a decision is useful when the people who must act on it know who is accountable for the next step.

Review the whole workflow

A technically convincing answer may still create work elsewhere. We look at how information arrives, how exceptions are resolved, how a person takes over, and how changes to the underlying business process reach the system. Training and knowledge maintenance belong in that conversation.

We also help distinguish a correctable implementation issue from a poor fit for the problem. A pilot can produce useful evidence even when the recommendation is to change the approach.

Give expansion a clear review point

Wider rollout changes the operating demands on a pilot. We help review the evidence alongside expected volumes, provider costs, review capacity, knowledge ownership, and the readiness of the teams affected. The next decision should have an accountable sponsor and clear conditions.

Where adoption or approval requirements need more work, our change management and practical governance services can help prepare those decisions.

Experience behind the advice

Our dental technology case describes an engagement that progressed from use-case definition and development to a limited live rollout in Canada. That hands-on experience informs the questions we bring to advisory work. Each new engagement has its own agreed responsibilities.

Use our Pilot Readiness Checklist to identify the prerequisites you already have and the questions that still need an owner.
answer: Authentia helps sponsors and delivery teams shape bounded AI pilots, evaluate tools and providers, and review the evidence before wider rollout. We clarify scope, responsibilities, evaluation criteria and operating implications. Your team or implementation partner builds and operates the solution, supported by practical advice and documented decisions.

title: Ongoing AI and digital change advisory
description: A continuing advisory relationship for leaders connecting AI priorities, digital change, investment decisions, adoption and practical governance.
body:
A consistent point of view as the work develops

AI decisions and digital changes rarely arrive in a neat sequence. A department proposes a new tool while another team is testing a workflow. A provider changes its product. A pilot reveals that the original problem needs a different approach. Leadership needs a way to connect those decisions to business priorities.

Ongoing advisory gives you continuity. Authentia works with your sponsor and relevant colleagues to review progress, challenge assumptions, and identify the decisions that need attention.

Set a useful remit

We begin by agreeing the purpose of the relationship: the business priorities it supports, the people involved, the decisions in scope, and a practical working cadence. The arrangement should fit the volume and complexity of decisions your organisation actually faces.

A retainer can complement a focused strategy project or support work already underway. We agree capacity, availability, deliverables, and responsibilities in the engagement scope.

What we can help with

  • Reviewing new AI opportunities and digital change priorities against an existing roadmap.
  • Preparing leadership discussions and investment decision briefs.
  • Assessing tool proposals and questions from implementation partners.
  • Reviewing pilot findings, adoption challenges, governance questions, and emerging dependencies.
  • Helping teams establish practical guidance for using AI in defined workflows.
  • Keeping a decision record so the reasoning behind choices remains visible.

Maintain a decision rhythm

A useful review starts with what has changed. What evidence arrived? Which assumption failed? What is blocked? Which decision would allow the next piece of work to move? We use that context to keep conversations focused and prepare clear next steps.

Between reviews, agreed advisory work can include examining a proposal, helping shape a brief, or working through an implementation question with the relevant team. The scope determines the level of involvement.

Connect leadership and delivery

Executives need to understand the value, cost, risk, and organisational implications of a choice. Delivery teams need specific requirements, decisions, and access to people who understand the workflow. We help translate between these perspectives and surface unresolved assumptions.

The aim is to leave your organisation with clearer decisions and stronger internal capability. Recommendations should be understandable and reusable, with a record of the evidence and reasoning behind them.

Adapt the roadmap as evidence improves

A roadmap is a set of choices made with the information available at the time. As projects progress, some opportunities will deserve more investment, others may need preparation, and some may cease to be worthwhile. We help review those changes without treating the original plan as a fixed commitment.

We can also help you identify patterns across projects: repeated data problems, unclear ownership, duplicated tools, or training needs that deserve a shared response.

Review value and adoption together

A continuing relationship provides a place to revisit the investment case as evidence arrives. We help sponsors compare expected benefits with operating effort, review capacity, adoption, and the outcomes observed in the workflow. Those reviews can identify a useful adjustment or a reason to change priorities.

We also help connect issues across initiatives. Repeated questions about ownership, manager support, or AI review may deserve a shared response through change management, workflow design, or practical governance.

Agree where advice ends and delivery begins

Your organisation retains responsibility for implementation, deployment, procurement, and operation. Authentia supports those responsibilities through the agreed advisory remit. Where specialist technical, legal, or sector expertise is needed, we help make the question clear for the appropriate owner.

If you are deciding between a focused project and a retainer, start with the next few decisions you expect to make. We can recommend a scope around those needs and explain what continuing support would add.

AI value and investment reviews can form part of the agreed advisory cadence, bringing evidence from individual initiatives into a portfolio-level decision about what to expand, revise, or stop.
answer: Authentia provides continuing advice for leaders managing AI priorities and digital change. We help review opportunities, investment assumptions, adoption evidence, governance questions and delivery decisions across initiatives. An agreed remit and working cadence give your team continuity, while your organisation retains authority over investment, implementation and operation.
